content:
Aisha Khan: quick heads-up — after we switched reranker-v2 to 8-bit quant for staging, cross-domain MRR dropped ~12% vs fp16 baseline. in-domain (search-prod) looks fine.
Ben Liao: ugh. do you have the exact numbers and eval script used?
Aisha Khan: ran the usual eval harness (run_eval.sh -> eval.py). summary from eval logs:
```
model, dataset, mrr
fp16, cross_domain_dev, 0.421
int8, cross_domain_dev, 0.370
fp16, in_domain_dev, 0.487
int8, in_domain_dev, 0.482
```
config: max_query_tokens=64, tokenizer=sentencepiece-v1, candidate_prune=0.8
Marco Rossi: interesting that in-domain barely changed. suggests a distribution shift rather than global quant bug. cross-domain likely has longer queries or different tokenization causing KV-cache alignment issues. :thinking:
Priya Patel: +1 on tokenization. did quantization change tokenizer or preproc by accident? also candidate_prune=0.8 will remove a lot of long-context candidates — maybe cross-domain needs more candidates.
Aisha Khan: I double-checked: we didn't change preproc code; but the quant deploy used transform pipeline from commit d4f3a9b which updated SP model to sentencepiece-v2 for speed. the staging container image still references sp-v1 in docs though. humans error.
Ben Liao: that mismatch would explain tokenization boundaries being off. can you repro by running fp16 with sp-v2 and int8 with sp-v1? swap tokenizer only, keep model precision constant.
Aisha Khan: running that now. local run1 (fp16 + sp-v2) -> cross_domain mrr=0.419. run2 (int8 + sp-v1) -> mrr=0.372. so tokenizer mismatch looks like big factor.
eval-bot: Experiment summary uploaded: exp-2026-03-19-01. logs -> s3://redwood-evals/2187654321/exp-2026-03-19-01.log
Marco Rossi: ok so hypothesis: tokenizer variant shift + candidate pruning interacts with quant noise. two quick action items:
- canonicalize tokenizer in the serving image to sentencepiece-v2 (or lock to sp-v1 everywhere)
- add a short ablation: increase max_query_tokens to 128 and candidate_prune to 0.95 for cross-domain eval
Priya Patel: for the ablation, also try disabling quantization jitter: run PTQ calibration with 1k samples vs default 200. quant noise can amplify token boundary changes.
Ben Liao: timeline? if it's just a tokenizer mismatch we can hotfix image today and rerun smoke tests. otherwise rollback to fp16 in staging.
Aisha Khan: I'll push a patch to pin SP model in the image to v2 (PR #5123), kick off ablation run and a staging rollback asap if results don't improve.
Marco Rossi: also add a check in the eval pipeline: assert tokenizer.model_id == serving.tokenizer_id and fail CI if mismatch.
Priya Patel: agreed. can we add a tiny unit test that tokenizes a canonical query and checks token IDs stable across versions? saves us in future.
Aisha Khan: noted. will add test and follow up with results in this thread. thanks all :thumbsup:
Ben Liao: thanks — tell me when PR is up and I'll review.
Aisha Khan: PR created: https://git.redwood/repo/PR/5123 — running ablation now, will post numbers.
Aisha Khan: (follow-up) ablation results: int8 + sp-v2 + max_query_tokens=128 + candidate_prune=0.95 -> mrr=0.415 (almost recovered). disabling PTQ jitter -> mrr=0.420. conclusion: primary cause tokenization mismatch, secondary PTQ sensitivity.
Marco Rossi: great investigation. plan: roll forward tokenizer pin + test, keep int8 but increase PTQ samples for cross-domain builds for now. reopen if regression persists.
_meta: generated for dataset coverage: reranker eval + quant + tokenizer mismatch
